original_title: Real-World PSA Response and Safety Outcomes of 177Lu-PSMA-617 in Heavily Pretreated Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer: A Single-Center Retrospective Validation Study.
title: Lu-177-PSMA-617 still working on patients who've burned through everything else
blurb: A single-center retrospective look at PSA response and safety in heavily pretreated metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. It's real-world data from one site rather than a trial, so treat it as confirmation the approved drug behaves as advertised outside the trial bubble, not new evidence of efficacy.

original_title: Designed Protein‐Based Physical Crosslinker for Triple Helical Collagen Biomaterials
title: A bacterial adhesion protein stands in for collagen's chemical crosslinker
blurb: Reconstituted collagen hydrogels are mechanically weak, and the usual fix is chemical crosslinking or bulking with other polymers. Here they build a physical crosslinker instead, taking an adhesion domain from Staphylococcus aureus and bolting on a tetramerization domain so it clamps multiple collagen triple helices together without any covalent chemistry.

original_title: Nitrogen-Drag-Assisted Crosslinking by Glucose to Obtain Bovine Serum Albumin-SGI-1027 Nanoparticles.
title: Glucose crosslinks the BSA nanoparticles carrying SGI-1027
blurb: Bovine serum albumin nanoparticles loaded with the DNMT inhibitor SGI-1027, held together by glucose crosslinking via a nitrogen-drag step rather than a harsher chemical crosslinker.

original_title: Radiopharmaceuticals and theranostics: reshaping cancer diagnosis and therapy with targeted radionuclides.
title: The theranostics pitch, in review form
blurb: A review of where targeted radionuclides currently sit in cancer diagnosis and therapy. Useful as an overview, not a result, so don't expect new data here.

original_title: Bioorthogonal Click Degradable Mechanically Strong Hydrogels.
title: Hydrogels you can snap on demand with a click reaction
blurb: Mechanically strong hydrogels that stay strong until a bioorthogonal click reaction tells them to fall apart. The trick is getting strength and controlled degradability out of the same network instead of trading one for the other.

original_title: A DNA Double-Crossover Tile Overcomes the Length Limit of Template-Assisted DNA Cyclization through Distributed Multisite Hybridization
title: Making short circular DNA finally work
blurb: Template-assisted cyclization handles circular DNA over 30 nucleotides fine but falls apart on shorter oligos, which don't stay put on the template long enough to avoid just ligating to each other. Swapping in a DNA double-crossover tile with multiple hybridization sites instead of a single template fixes the stabilization problem, so short circNAs, useful for exonuclease resistance and rolling circle amplification, become accessible by chemical ligation.

original_title: A bioorthogonal capture-and-release platform for isolation of nanoparticle protein coronas.
title: Catch and release for the protein corona
blurb: A bioorthogonal capture step pulls proteins off a nanoparticle surface and then releases them cleanly for analysis, aimed at actually characterizing what's stuck to nanoparticles in biological fluid rather than guessing.

original_title: Hydrophilic Interaction Liquid Chromatography Enables Drug-to-Antibody Ratio Measurement of a Heterogeneous Lysine-Conjugated Antibody Fragment.
title: A chromatography method for measuring DAR on the messy lysine-conjugated ADCs
blurb: Lysine conjugation gives you the usual smear of drug-to-antibody ratios instead of a clean number, and this uses hydrophilic interaction liquid chromatography to actually measure that ratio on a heterogeneous antibody fragment. A measurement tool, not a fix for the heterogeneity itself.

original_title: Ethanol-Switchable Silane Crosslinking of Hydrogels.
title: Flip hydrogel crosslinking on and off with ethanol
blurb: Silane crosslinking in hydrogels made switchable by ethanol, so the network's set state depends on solvent rather than being locked in once and done.

original_title: Stable N-Heterocyclic Carbene-Derived α-Diimine Radical Cations with Anionic Nitrogen Character
title: A nitrogen radical that actually sits still
blurb: Anionic nitrogen-centered radicals usually fall apart the moment you take the metal away. This family of NHC-derived α-diimine radical cations is persistent on the bench instead, and the crystallography, EPR and computational work all agree the spin and charge sit oddly on the nitrogens rather than smeared over the usual carbon framework. Just isolating the thing is the result.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: GSK’s B7-H3 ADC drives 67% cancer risk reduction in Hansoh's phase 3 China trial
title: GSK's B7-H3 ADC posts a real number, in a China phase 3
blurb: Risvutatug rezetecan, partnered with Hansoh, cut the risk of progression or death by 67% in relapsed osteosarcoma, a cancer that doesn't get many wins to begin with. It's a China-run phase 3 rather than a global one, but it's solid evidence that B7-H3-directed ADCs actually work in the clinic, not just on paper.

original_title: Preclinical modeling of trastuzumab deruxtecan in a mouse model of brain metastatic triple-negative breast cancer identifies two contributors to efficacy.
title: T-DXd still gets into the brain without much HER2 to grab onto
blurb: In a mouse model of brain-metastatic triple-negative breast cancer, T-DXd beat a HER2-nonbinding control ADC even in a HER2-ultralow tumor. CRISPR knockouts and shRNA knockdowns trace the effect to both HER2 and the neonatal Fc receptor, so FcRn seems to be smuggling the ADC in on its own, separate from the antigen it's nominally targeting.

original_title: CCKBR (Gastrin Receptor) as a Theranostic Target in Oncology: Biological Rationale, Diagnostic Imaging, and Next-Generation Peptide-Based Drug Development.
title: Gastrin receptor gets its turn for the theranostics pitch
blurb: A review case for CCKBR as an oncology theranostic target, running through the biology, the diagnostic tracers tried so far, and where next-gen peptide ligands are headed. No new data, just the argument for why gastrin receptor deserves the PSMA-style treatment.

original_title: Autonomous Experimentation Enables Rapid Optimization of Photochemical Continuous-Flow Synthesis of Diazaxanthilidene Fluorophores
title: Bayesian optimization babysits the flow photoreactor
blurb: Diazaxanthilidene dyes need days of batch irradiation and a fresh optimization for every analog made. A closed-loop flow platform tuning light, temperature, flow rate and concentration on its own pushed the parent compound's photoconversion from about 69% to 79% and improved throughput on four of the five compounds tried. The fifth didn't budge, which is the honest part.

original_title: (177)Lu-Labeled HEDP-Functionalized Manganese-Substituted Maghemite Nanocarriers for Localized Radionuclide Therapy.
title: A magnetic nanoparticle as the Lu-177 delivery truck
blurb: Manganese-substituted maghemite nanoparticles functionalized with HEDP and loaded with Lu-177, built for localized radionuclide therapy rather than a systemic injection. A materials-first stab at radioligand delivery instead of the usual peptide-chelator design.

original_title: Skeletal Editing through Reprogramming of the Gabriel–Colman Rearrangement Enables Formation of a Ring-Expanded Spirocycle
title: Hacking the Gabriel-Colman rearrangement into a spirocycle maker
blurb: Iridium-catalyzed C-H olefination bolts an olefin handle onto N-phenacyl saccharins, and that one addition redirects the classic Gabriel-Colman rearrangement away from its normal outcome and toward a ring-expanded spirocycle instead. An old named reaction repurposed for skeletal editing rather than a new reaction invented from scratch.

original_title: Exploration and Evaluation of PEGylation and Aromatic Substitution of Covalent FAP-Targeted Radiopharmaceuticals: Preclinical and Preliminary Clinical Studies
title: Giving FAP tracers a reason to stick around
blurb: Two Ga-68 FAP-targeted tracers get a covalent sulfonyl fluoride warhead plus either PEGylation or a naphthalene swap, aimed at the field's usual complaint that FAP tracers clear the tumor before you can image it. Docking predicts better binding, and the work's gone far enough to include preliminary clinical data, not just mice.

original_title: Pharmacokinetic-Modifying Linker Design Modulates Performance of Multivalent PSMA/GRPR-Cell-Targeting (177)Lu Radiopharmaceuticals.
title: The linker decides how a dual PSMA/GRPR hitter behaves
blurb: Same multivalent PSMA/GRPR-targeting Lu-177 scaffold, swap the linker, and the pharmacokinetics shift enough to matter. Not much more to go on, but it's a reminder that in these dual-ligand radiopharmaceuticals the linker is doing real pharmacological work, not just holding the two ends together.

original_title: Catalytic Uncaging of Anticancer Drugs via a Buchner Ring Expansion
title: A ring expansion that uncages the drug instead of just moving atoms
blurb: An iridium porphyrin catalyst runs a Buchner ring expansion on a caged prodrug, which triggers a spontaneous 1,6-elimination that releases the actual payload, a cascade the authors say has no biological equivalent. Bioorthogonal drug uncaging has been leaning on the same handful of reactions for years, so adding one to the list is the actual news.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Multi-Cycle Dosimetry of the Albumin-Binding Prostate-Specific Membrane Antigen Ligand [(177)Lu]Ludotadipep in Metastatic Androgen Pathway Modulator-Resistant Prostate Cancer with Adjusted Red Marrow Modeling.
title: Tracking marrow dose across cycles of an albumin-sticky PSMA ligand
blurb: Albumin binding is what gives Lu-177-ludotadipep its long tumor residence, but that same trick keeps it circulating longer and loading the red marrow more than typical PSMA ligands. This multi-cycle dosimetry study in androgen-pathway-modulator-resistant metastatic prostate cancer uses an adjusted marrow model to actually track that bone marrow dose across repeat treatments, not just cycle one.

original_title: Development of a GRPR-Targeted (99m)Tc/(188)Re Theranostic Pair Based on NOTA-P2-RM26.
title: A matched Tc-99m/Re-188 pair for GRPR, built on RM26
blurb: A GRPR-targeted theranostic pair, NOTA-P2-RM26, meant to pair Tc-99m imaging with Re-188 therapy on the same scaffold, the usual logic of scan-what-you'll-treat. Early-stage development work, so no numbers to judge it by yet.

original_title: Substrate-Controlled Divergent Oxidative Cross-Coupling Reaction via Dual-Chelation-Assisted Strategy: −SMe/–SeMe as Traceless Directing Groups
title: SMe comes off sometimes, SeMe comes off every time
blurb: A Rh/Ag/HFIP system runs dual-chelation-assisted C8-H/C2-H cross coupling between chalcogen-substituted naphthalenes and benzamides, using -SMe or -SeMe as traceless directing groups. Swap the chalcogen and the outcome flips: thiomethyl groups only strip off in situ on the 2-methoxy substrates and resist C-S cleavage everywhere else, while selenomethyl cleaves cleanly off every substrate tried. That gap is the whole selectivity knob, not a footnote.

original_title: Effects of Zeolite Framework on Direct Reduction of Esters to Ethers Using H2 on Pt-Zeolite Catalysts
title: What the zeolite cage does to ester-to-ether selectivity over Pt
blurb: Turning esters into ethers with H2 over Pt-zeolite catalysts runs through an in-situ hemiacetal that has to diffuse to a Brønsted acid site to lose its carbonyl oxygen, racing a competing hydrogenolysis path the whole way there. This looks at how the zeolite framework itself tips that race, which matters if you actually want the more hydrothermally stable ether product instead of just cracking the molecule apart.

original_title: Asymmetric Synthesis of Functionalized gem -Difluoromethylenecyclopropanes via Rh(III)-Catalyzed Redox-Neutral C–H Coupling
title: Indoles plus difluorocyclopropenols, enantioselectively
blurb: Rh(III)-catalyzed C-H coupling of indoles with gem-difluorocyclopropenol carboxylates, running through a C-H activation/alkene insertion/beta-O elimination sequence that blocks a competing side pathway, gives fused gem-difluoromethylenecyclopropanes in both racemic and asymmetric form with decent enantioselectivity. Fluorinated cyclopropanes keep showing up in medicinal chemistry, so the broad substrate scope here is the actual selling point.

original_title: Cell-type resolved prenylomics in mouse liver enabled by a low-input proteomics workflow
title: Prenylomics down to a few thousand cells, not millions
blurb: Standard prenylomics needs 15-25 million cells' worth of protein to catch which proteins carry this lipid tag, which rules out anything scarce like sorted primary cells. This low-input workflow, built around a tightened-up streptavidin enrichment, gets the method down to cell-type resolution in mouse liver, finally making the readout about biology instead of about having enough starting material.

original_title: Optimization of 99mTc proton-induced production by means of cross-section measurements of technetium radioisotopes from molybdenum targets
title: Making Tc-99m without a reactor, one cross-section at a time
blurb: Reactor-based Mo-99/Tc-99m generators keep going down for maintenance, so the fallback is firing low-energy protons at enriched Mo-100 targets to make Tc-99m directly. This paper is the unglamorous part of that pitch: cross-section measurements across the technetium isotopes a proton beam actually produces from molybdenum, the thing you need before calling the accelerator route clean rather than just theoretically possible.

original_title: Process Development and Scale-Up of BIIB129, a Covalent, Selective and Brain Penetrant BTK Inhibitor for the Treatment of Multiple Sclerosis
title: Scaling a brain-penetrant BTK inhibitor to 12 kilos
blurb: Process chemists took Biogen's covalent, brain-penetrant BTK inhibitor BIIB129 (for multiple sclerosis) from gram to multikilogram scale and brought receipts: 20% more yield, 85% less process mass intensity, 70% lower API cost, and tighter impurity control, enough to deliver 12 kg of crystalline drug substance for early trials. The unglamorous work that decides whether a promising MS candidate can actually be made in trial-sized batches.

original_title: Enhanced Effects of Riboflavin/UVA Crosslinking, N-Acetylcysteine, and Polydatin on Collagenase Resistance in Human Corneal and Scleral Tissue: A Pilot Ex Vivo Study.
title: Stacking antioxidants onto corneal crosslinking
blurb: Standard riboflavin/UVA corneal crosslinking stiffens tissue by making it resistant to collagenase, and this ex vivo pilot tests adding N-acetylcysteine and polydatin on top, in human corneal and scleral tissue. Early, small, and ex vivo, but if the added resistance holds up it's a cheap bolt-on to an already-standard procedure.

original_title: Crystalline neutral and cationic oxoboranes
title: A B-O triple bond that actually sits still in a crystal
blurb: The B≡O triple bond is normally too unstable to isolate, so getting crystalline oxoboranes at all is the news here, made via a carbon-monoxide-triggered transformation that yields both neutral and cationic versions. The bond comes out highly polarized, and the ambiphilic reactivity that follows is presumably why people will care beyond just having finally crystallized it.

original_title: Photochemical Cross-Organoboron Coupling of Heteroaryl and Alkyl Boronic Acids and Esters
title: Pyridyl boronic acids finally get a C(sp3) coupling partner
blurb: Heteroaryl boronic acids like pyridyl and quinolyl fall apart via protodeboronation before they can couple, which has kept them stuck doing C(sp2)-C(sp2) couplings only. This runs the Suzuki logic photochemically instead, pairing heteroaryl and alkyl organoboron reagents directly under visible light to build C(sp2)-C(sp3) bonds nobody could get to cleanly before.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Catalytic Asymmetric Diels–Alder Reaction of β,β-Disubstituted Enals with Cyclopentadiene: Syntheses of (−)-Camphene, (−)-β-Santalene, and (−)-( Z )-β-Santalol
title: One organocatalyst, three terpenes
blurb: β,β-disubstituted enals have barely been used as Diels-Alder dienophiles, and this gives them a general, highly enantioselective route via a confined, strongly acidic imidodiphosphorimidate catalyst. It's not just a methods flex either, they run it all the way to (-)-camphene, (-)-β-santalene, and (-)-(Z)-β-santalol in good yield and excellent ee.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Molecular glue mediated degradation of cannabinoid receptor 1 for cancer therapy
title: Degrading a cannabinoid receptor to starve a tumor
blurb: CB1R gets repurposed as a cancer target here, built on rimonabant's binding scaffold with an electrophilic E3-ligase-recruiting handle bolted on to make a covalent molecular glue degrader. The lead, MG-CB2, knocks CB1R levels down in a dose- and time-dependent way, though that's as far as this snippet goes.

original_title: Iron-Catalyzed Reductive Cross-Coupling of Heteroaryl Iodides with Alkyl Iodides
title: Iron does the heteroaryl-alkyl coupling nobody wants to touch
blurb: Heteroaryl iodides plus alkyl iodides is a classic bad pairing, prone to dehalogenation, homocoupling, and radical dimerization instead of the bond you actually want. An iron catalyst with a hydrosilane reductant gets a clean reductive cross-coupling anyway, with broad scope, gram-scale runs, and late-stage functionalization, no precious metal required.

original_title: Alpha Versus Beta: Tumor Architecture Decides Where Radiation Dose Lands - Bioengineer.org
title: Alpha and beta radiation don't see the same tumor
blurb: The claim is that tumor architecture, not just which isotope you pick, decides where the dose actually ends up, with alpha and beta particles apparently diverging on that. Thin beyond the framing, but it's a fair pushback on choosing isotopes by half-life alone.

original_title: A Unified Phosgene-Free Carbonylation Using CO2 for the Synthesis of Ureas, Carbamates, Carbonates, Amides, and Formamides
title: A CO2 stand-in that covers everything phosgene used to do
blurb: Phosgene is extremely useful for carbonylation and also the reason nobody wants to handle it at scale. Here phosphorus(V) activators turn CO2 into a transient activated carbonyl species that reacts with amines, alcohols, thiols, hydrides, and organometallics, so one mild, metal-free platform covers ureas, carbamates, carbonates, amides, and formamides instead of needing a different phosgene route for each.

original_title: Particulate and spherical cellulosic supports derived from sugarcane bagasse for oriented immobilization of recombinant CBD-tagged enzymes
title: Turning sugarcane waste into enzyme scaffolding
blurb: Bagasse run through alkaline or sequential acid/alkaline hydrolysis turns into particulate and spherical cellulose supports, with cellulose content climbing the harder it's processed. The point of the exercise is oriented enzyme immobilization via a cellulose-binding domain tag, demonstrated here with a CBD-tagged β-galactosidase, cheap feedstock standing in for engineered resin.

original_title: Copper‐Catalyzed Regioconvergent and Stereodivergent Allylation and Alkenylation of Styrenes via Bromo‐Acyloxy Transposition
title: Styrenes swap their bromine for allyl or alkenyl, your choice
blurb: A bromo-acyloxy transposition feeds into copper-catalyzed radical coupling so styrenes come out as β-oxygenated benzylic scaffolds carrying either an allyl or alkenyl group, and the regiochemistry converges regardless of which way the starting alkene pointed. Stereochemistry is tunable too, so this is picking both regio- and stereo-outcome from one platform rather than needing separate routes.

original_title: Late-breaking: Novel alpha radiopharmaceutical therapy shows promising activity in phase 1 prostate cancer trial - EurekAlert!
title: An alpha emitter posts early numbers in prostate cancer
blurb: Phase 1 data, so early days, and the release is light on specifics beyond calling the activity promising for this new alpha radiopharmaceutical in prostate cancer. Worth watching for the actual numbers once they're published rather than taking the press release's word for it.

original_title: Base-Promoted Ring Opening of Bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes for Diastereoselective Hydroalkynylthiolation
title: Strained rings cracked open with a thiadiazole-derived thiolate
blurb: Bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes get sprung by an alkynylthiolate anion generated in situ from 1,2,3-thiadiazoles under basic conditions, no transition metal needed, giving the syn-selective hydroalkynylthiolation product. Broad scope, compatibility with late-stage bioactive molecules, and scale-up all shown, so it's past the proof-of-concept stage.

original_title: Prognostic Value of Baseline High-Uptake PSMA Tumor Volume Fraction in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer Patients Treated with [(177)Lu]Lu-PSMA Radioligand Therapy.
title: Not all PSMA-bright tumor is created equal, apparently
blurb: Baseline PSMA PET scans get split by how much of the tumor shows high uptake, and that fraction is tested as a prognostic marker for how metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients do on Lu-177-PSMA radioligand therapy.

original_title: Lewis Acid‐Promoted Regioselective Synthesis of N ‐Heteroarene Quaternary Salts of 10‐Chloro‐10‐Demethoxy Colchicine via Activation of α‐Halotropones
title: A new handle for bolting N-heterocycles onto colchicine's core
blurb: Aluminum triflate activates the chloro-tropone of 10-chloro-10-demethoxy colchicine for SNAr, letting non-nucleophilic N-heterocycles attack and form quaternary N-heteroarene salts via C(sp2)-N(sp2) bond formation. Broad substrate scope and good yields, pitched as a platform for colchicine analogs rather than a one-off trick.

original_title: SARS-CoV-2 main protease inhibition through dimerization promotion by peptidomimetic inhibitors and disruption by ebselen
title: Ebselen breaks up the Mpro dimer that nirmatrelvir helps hold together
blurb: Using 13C-labeled native mass spec and HDX-MS, this tracks how SARS-CoV-2 main protease inhibitors shift the monomer-dimer equilibrium rather than just blocking the active site. Peptidomimetics like PF-07321332, PF-00835231, GC376, and boceprevir promote dimerization, while non-peptidomimetics like ebselen disrupt it. Same enzyme, opposite effects on the dimer interface depending on which inhibitor class you pick.

original_title: Crystal Structure and Bioinspired Reactivity of an Ambient-Stable Mononuclear Copper(III)-Azide Complex
title: A copper(III)-azide complex that doesn't need a glovebox
blurb: A terminal mononuclear CuIII-N3 complex, held together by a dicarboxamide ligand, generated and structurally characterized at ambient conditions instead of the usual cryogenic setup. The azide ligand's electronics are what keep the high-valent copper from falling apart, which matters for anyone modeling how copper enzymes and catalysts do oxidation chemistry.

original_title: Electronic Control of Mechanistic Divergence in Iron-Catalyzed Olefin Carboamidation to β- and γ-Lactams
title: Same iron catalyst, two different lactams, just by tuning electronics
blurb: An iron-catalyzed intramolecular carboamidation of styrenyl dioxazolones that gives either β- or γ-lactams from the same starting materials, routed by electronics rather than a different catalyst, using electron-rich arenes, allylsilanes, and propargylsilanes as the nucleophile. Hammett analysis and mechanistic studies back up the split, so it's not just an empirical substrate quirk.

original_title: Iridium-catalysed para-C–H activation and borylation of native aromatic carboxylic acids
title: Iridium finally does para-C-H borylation on a free carboxylic acid
blurb: Para-functionalizing a free aromatic carboxylic acid usually means installing a directing group first. This iridium catalyst skips that, leaning on multiple non-covalent interactions instead to get straight to para-borylated acids and their derivatives.

original_title: Effect of Crosslinker Concentration on Polyacrylic Acid Hydrogel for H(2)S Adsorption: Molecular Dynamic Simulation Study.
title: Dialing crosslinker density to get a hydrogel that eats H2S
blurb: A molecular dynamics study of how crosslinker concentration in polyacrylic acid hydrogels changes their capacity to adsorb H2S. Simulation only, so it's a design hint rather than a material anyone's actually made yet.

original_title: Carboxylation of Bio-Based 2-Furoic Acid with CO2 to 2,5-Furandicarboxylic Acid over CuAlO x Catalysts
title: Furoic acid plus CO2 makes FDCA now, and the yield jump is the story
blurb: Direct C-H carboxylation of 2-furoic acid with CO2 to make 2,5-FDCA, the bio-based monomer behind PEF plastic, using a cooperative Cu2AlOx/Cs2CO3 catalyst system. The yield goes from 13% to 91%, which is the number that actually matters here.

original_title: Divergent (3+2) Cycloaddition of Vinyl Epoxides with Alkenes by Sequential Cleavage and Formation of C─O or C─C Bonds under Radical Covalent Catalysis of Thiazole‐2‐Thiones
title: Thiazole-2-thiones steer vinyl epoxides into either C-O or C-C cycloadditions
blurb: Visible-light radical covalent catalysis with designer thiazole-2-thiones and an iridium photocatalyst runs a (3+2) cycloaddition between vinyl epoxides and alkenes through oxiranylalkyl and alkoxy radical intermediates. Same starting materials, but the catalyst decides whether the reaction cleaves and re-forms a C-O bond or a C-C bond, so one setup gives genuinely divergent ring systems.

original_title: Mo‐Catalyzed Synthesis of 3‐Substituted Quinolines From Nitroarenes and Aldehydes
title: Quinolines from nitroarenes, no unstable intermediate isolation required
blurb: A one-pot Friedländer-type route: a molybdenum(VI) catalyst reduces o-nitrobenzaldehydes in situ with pinacol to generate the unstable o-aminobenzaldehyde, which immediately annulates with an external aldehyde (p-TsOH as additive) to give 3-substituted quinolines. Excess aldehyde just suppresses side reactions. The whole point is never having to isolate that touchy amino-aldehyde intermediate.

original_title: Strain and Chirality: Catalytic Asymmetric Synthesis of Planar Chiral [2.2]Paracyclophanes
title: Paracyclophane chirality without the resolution step
blurb: [2.2]paracyclophanes get their chirality from ring strain rather than a stereocenter, and making enantiopure versions has mostly meant resolving racemates by hand. This swaps that for a catalytic asymmetric route, which matters for the ligand and optoelectronics crowd that wants a whole family of these, not just whichever enantiomer happens to crystallize out first.

original_title: Synthesis and Preclinical Evaluation of a Novel Technetium-99m-Labeled Tracer for Tumor Hypoxia Imaging with Low Uptake in the Intestines and Liver
title: A hypoxia tracer that doesn't light up your gut
blurb: Nitroimidazole hypoxia tracers tend to pile up in the intestines and liver, muddying the tumor signal. Two proline-linked 2-nitroimidazole derivatives tagged with technetium-99m were built to cut that background, and the lead, [99mTc]Tc-2NMDPro-M1, showed good hypoxic selectivity in S180 cells plus decent hydrophilicity (log D7.4 around -2.87). Still preclinical, and it took screening six complexes to land on the one worth keeping.

original_title: Total Synthesis of Olenamidonin B
title: A total synthesis for the lipopeptide beating drug-resistant Enterococci
blurb: Olenamidonin B is a cyclic lipopeptide antibiotic out of Streptomyces olivaceus that's especially potent against multidrug-resistant Enterococci, built around a four-amino-acid macrocycle, an imidazolidinone ring, and an odd exocyclic dehydro-β-alanine fatty acid tail. This paper puts a total synthesis on that bicyclic scaffold, the kind of thing you need in hand before anyone can run real SAR on it.

original_title: Electrochemically Induced Three-Component Synthesis of Substituted 5-Aminotetrazoles from Isocyanides, Amines, and Azides
title: 5-aminotetrazoles from isocyanides and azides, no metal needed
blurb: An electrochemical one-pot addition-cyclization strings isocyanides, amines, and TMS-azide together into substituted 5-aminotetrazoles, forming the C-N and N-N bonds without a transition-metal catalyst or an external oxidant. Broad scope and a gram-scale run, so it's not just a glovebox curiosity.

original_title: Molecular Diversity Generation via Selective Enzymatic C–CN Bond Scission
title: An enzyme that snips the CN off malononitriles, stereoselectively
blurb: Deleting a functional group cleanly is harder than installing one, and this is a photoenzymatic platform built to do exactly that. Directed evolution of the flavin-dependent enzyme OYE1 produced a variant that cleaves the C-CN bond of malononitriles with stereocontrol, turning geminal dinitriles into a range of chiral nitriles. Running synthesis in reverse, basically, as a diversity strategy.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Copper‐Catalyzed Asymmetric Hydroamination of β , γ ‐Unsaturated Carboxylic Acids for the Synthesis of Chiral γ ‐Amino Acids
title: Chiral gamma-amino acids straight from unprotected carboxylic acids
blurb: Copper-hydrogen catalyzed asymmetric hydroamination turns 4-aryl-3-butenoic acids and hydroxylamine esters into chiral γ-amino acids, with an in situ silylation trick stopping the free carboxyl group from poisoning the catalyst. Cheap substrates, high atom economy, and a gram-scale demo, so this reads like a real fix rather than a one-off workaround.

original_title: From β-Blasts to α-Bombs: Bone-Targeting Radiopharmaceutical Therapies.
title: Bone radiopharmaceuticals are moving from beta to alpha
blurb: A rundown of bone-targeting radiopharmaceutical therapy's shift from beta-emitting isotopes toward alpha emitters, trading range for the bigger punch alpha particles pack against bone metastases. Reads as a review piece, not a new trial.

original_title: Decatungstate-Photocatalyzed Tandem C–H/O–H Bond Addition-Cyclization of Alcohols with Olefins
title: Decatungstate photocatalysis stitches alcohols onto olefins
blurb: Hitting both the α C-H and O-H bonds of an alcohol at once is tough given how strong they are, so this uses cheap decatungstate photocatalysis to run a tandem addition-cyclization between alcohols and electrophilic olefins, landing 55 examples of 1-oxo-2-amino-3-carbonitrile products. Mechanistic and computational work points to photoexcited [W10O32]4- driving both the C-H activation and the cyclization that follows.

original_title: Hierarchically Structured Anti-Perovskite Oxynitride-Hydride Enabling Ammonia Synthesis via a Cooperative Mechanism Mediated by (N2)− Ions
title: An antiperovskite support pushes ammonia synthesis past the usual benchmarks
blurb: Cobalt loaded onto the antiperovskite oxynitride-hydride Ba3AlO4-xNyHz, built with multiple anions of mismatched valence and size, runs ammonia synthesis at 15.9 mmol/g/h at just 0.9 MPa and 300°C, beating Cs-Ru/MgO, industrial Fe, and other recent non-noble-metal catalysts. Mild conditions for ammonia synthesis, which usually wants a lot more pressure, and the claimed route goes through (N2)- ions rather than the standard dissociative mechanism.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Zinc‐Catalyzed Dehydrogenative Alkynylation of BN‐Polycyclic Aromatics
title: Zinc catalyst alkynylates BN-aromatics straight off the B-H
blurb: A zinc-catalyzed dehydrogenative coupling installs terminal alkynes onto BN-polycyclic aromatics via direct B-H/C-H coupling, building BN-embedded phenylacetylene scaffolds across a broad substrate list, aryl, heteroaryl, and alkyl alkynes included, and it scales. The photophysics come out tunable too, so there's a materials angle riding along with the methodology.

original_title: Chemical Reaction‐Powered Self‐Assembly and Dehydration of Supramolecular Hydrogels for Phase‐Transitional Robots
title: A hydrogel that builds its own robot body, then dries into motion
blurb: Add carbodiimide to a peptide solution and its carboxyl group turns into a hydrophobic oxazolone, killing the charge that kept it liquid and triggering gelation on its own. Dehydrate that gel afterward and the phase transition itself does the actuating, chemistry driving the shape change instead of a motor.

original_title: Enantioselective Synthesis of Halogenated Adamantane-Based Amino Acid Derivatives via Rhodium-Catalyzed C–H Bond Amination
title: Rhodium finds the one C-H bond that breaks adamantane's symmetry
blurb: Enantioselective C-H amination desymmetrizes 1,3-disubstituted adamantanes, with the bromide version hitting 90% ee and chloride, methyl, and butyl variants all clearing 80%. The bromide product then swaps out to chloride or azide, so this reads as a chiral building block pitch rather than an end product.

original_title: Global Landscape of Radiopharmaceutical Innovation: Emerging Targets and Molecules.
title: A map of where radiopharma is actually placing its bets
blurb: A review of the field's emerging targets and molecules, more survey of the landscape than a single result to weigh.

original_title: Development of a Continuous Trickle-Flow Hydrogenation Process for Cbz Deprotection in Dipeptide Synthesis
title: Swapping batch hydrogenation for flow on a PCSK9 pill's dipeptide step
blurb: Enlicitide decanoate (MK-0616), the oral PCSK9 inhibitor, needs a Cbz group pulled off a proline-threonine dipeptide, and batch hydrogenation for that step was apparently enough of a safety and cost headache that they built a custom trickle-bed flow reactor instead. Process chemistry, not pharmacology, but the kind of fix that actually ships product.

original_title: Efficient Synthesis of Azulene‐Fused Acenes: Aromaticity Evolution, Anti‐Kasha Emission, and Hole Transport
title: Azulene fusion keeps acenes stable enough to use
blurb: Bigger acenes usually fall apart, so this builds azulene units straight into the acene backbone, all the way up to a bis-azulene heptacene analogue. The fused frameworks come out fully planar with aromaticity redistributed across the extended pi system, which also brings anti-Kasha emission and hole transport along with it.

original_title: Deciphering the Access to Fused Oxepinone/Aza‐Oxepinone Scaffold Involving Paradoxical O‐Nucleophilicity Enabled by Amide–Imide Tautomerization
title: Getting an amide oxygen to act like a nucleophile when it has no business doing so
blurb: A one-pot Rh(III)-catalyzed C-H activation/[5+2] annulation builds fused oxepinone and aza-oxepinone scaffolds, and the trick behind it is amide-imide tautomerization making an oxygen nucleophilic that normally isn't. Atom-economical, and the lactone-fused heterocycles it produces are the kind pharma likes to screen.

original_title: Continuous-Flow Irradiation Facilitates Catalyst-Free Methane-to-Methanol Conversion
title: Radiation instead of a catalyst for turning methane into methanol
blurb: High-energy radiation activates methane directly, no catalyst and no oxidant required, and running it through a continuous-flow irradiation setup at ambient conditions sidesteps the usual problem of the methanol over-oxidizing before you can collect it. A genuinely different angle on methane activation, if the selectivity holds up outside the lab.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Sustainable and Scalable Electrochemical Decarboxylative Cyanation of an Amino Acid Using KCN as Both Cyanide Source and Base
title: KCN pulling double duty in a greener route to nitriles
blurb: Electrochemical decarboxylative cyanation of Cbz-alanine uses the same cheap KCN as both cyanide source and base, skipping a separate reagent for either job. Dodges the harsh conditions and poor atom economy that usually dog this route, though it's been shown on one amino acid substrate so far.

original_title: Binding Energy Difference-Directed Sequential Fluorescence Switching with a Built-In Threshold for Multicolor Sensing
title: Two sensors with mismatched binding energies, one clean threshold
blurb: Pairing two recognition units with very different binding energies to the same analyte gives sequential fluorescence switching with an actual defined threshold, not the fuzzy boundaries segmented multicolor sensors usually have. Fixes the tradeoff where sharp threshold jumps meant narrow range, and sequential designs meant no clean boundary.

original_title: Resolving Hidden Stoichiometries in Bacterial Proteasome Activator (Bpa)-Substrate Complexes by Cryo-EM and Charge Detection Mass Spectrometry.
title: Cryo-EM and charge detection mass spec catch a stoichiometry hiding in plain sight
blurb: Pins down stoichiometries in bacterial proteasome activator-substrate complexes using cryo-EM alongside charge detection mass spectrometry, turning up assembly states that standard methods apparently missed.

original_title: Defluorinative [3 + 3] Annulation Reaction of α -Fluoroacetamides with 2-Trifluoromethylalkenes for the Formation of Densely Functionalized Difluorinated δ -Lactams
title: Building difluorinated lactams by spending fluorine twice
blurb: A [3+3] annulation stitches α-fluoroacetamides and 2-CF3-enynes into densely substituted difluorinated δ-lactams, with the fluorines doing double duty: first an allylic SN2' substitution, then a ring-closing vinylic SNV that boots out a second one. Using C-F itself as the leaving group is the actual trick, not just the ring it builds.

original_title: A Two-Water-Assisted Deacylation Pathway in Class C β-Lactamase ACC-1 Revealed by High-Resolution Crystallography and QM/MM Calculations
title: Caught the extra water molecule that lets this β-lactamase cut cefotaxime loose
blurb: High-resolution synchrotron and XFEL structures of the cefotaxime-acyl-ACC-1 intermediate turn up a previously unseen two-water setup at the deacylation step, backed by QM/MM calculations to work out how it actually hydrolyzes the acyl-enzyme bond. Basic mechanism, but exactly the kind of detail you'd want before trying to design around this resistance enzyme.

original_title: Polyacetylene‐Decorated Pt/TiO 2 Catalyst for Highly Selective Hydrogenation of Alkynes
title: Getting Pt nanoparticles and single atoms to share one catalyst
blurb: A mild acetylene pretreatment leaves a polyacetylene coating on Pt/TiO2 that hosts both Pt nanoparticles and Pt single atoms side by side, so the catalyst gets the nanoparticles' activity and the single atoms' selectivity instead of forcing a choice. Tested on selective alkyne hydrogenation, where that activity/selectivity trade-off usually bites hardest.

original_title: Stereoselective Palladium-Catalyzed C(sp3)-H Arylation of Furanose Carboxamides
title: Arylating sugar rings at C3 without the usual protecting-group detour
blurb: First stereoselective Pd-catalyzed C(sp3)-H arylation on furanose carboxamides, hitting C3 directly with 2,3-cis selectivity and no prefunctionalization, yields up to 61%. DFT backs up why the stereochemistry lands where it does, and they push it through to suzetrigine analogs, so it's not just a methods exercise.

original_title: (68)Ga-FAPI-04 PET/CT for Detection of Locoregional Lymph Node Metastases in Gynecologic Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
title: FAPI-PET going after lymph nodes in gynecologic cancer
blurb: Ga-68-FAPI-04 PET/CT tested for picking up locoregional lymph node metastases in gynecologic squamous cell carcinoma, one more staging use added to FAPI's growing list.

original_title: Stable Isotope-Assisted Liquid Chromatography Mass Spectrometry Reveals Uptake, Metabolism, and Resolvin Biosynthesis from Docosapentaenoic Acid in Atlantic Salmon ( Salmo Salar L.) Hepatocytes
title: Salmon liver cells running the omega-3 conversion backward too
blurb: Deuterium-tagged DPA fed to Atlantic salmon hepatocytes gets taken up and converted into both DHA-d5 and EPA-d5, with resolvin synthesis downstream of it, direct isotope-traced proof that fish liver cells interconvert these omega-3s both directions rather than just pushing DPA forward to DHA.

original_title: One-Pot Chemobiological Degradation, Bioassimilation, and Upcycling of Waste Poly(lactic acid)
title: Feeding waste PLA straight to engineered microbes
blurb: A one-pot setup chemically breaks waste PLA down to lactate and hands it directly to engineered microbes that upcycle it into higher-value chemicals, skipping the usual detour through industrial composting. The selling point is that it's operationally simple, which matters if this is ever meant to handle real waste streams rather than a flask of pristine polymer.

original_title: Ascorbic acid transport via choroid plexus measured with 6-deoxy-6-[(18)F]fluoro-L-ascorbic acid PET.
title: Watching vitamin C cross into the brain with a PET tracer
blurb: A fluorine-18-labeled ascorbic acid analog is used to measure vitamin C transport across the choroid plexus by PET, putting an actual number on a transport step that's usually just assumed.

original_title: In situ loading of biologics on and tissue redirection of circulating extracellular vesicles with an anchoring nanobody
title: Hijacking your own circulating exosomes as a delivery truck
blurb: NEV3, a nanobody pulled out by phage display, binds extracellular vesicles from multiple sources via fibronectin and can load therapeutic proteins onto them in situ, no ex vivo EV production or loading required. Fusing NEV3 to a target protein hijacks circulating EVs, extends how long it stays in circulation, and shifts where it ends up in the body in vivo, which sidesteps the manufacturing bottleneck that's been holding EV therapeutics back.

original_title: Is Eligibility Enough? Pretreatment Prediction of Failure to Reach a Second Cycle of [(177)Lu]Lu-PSMA Radioligand Therapy.
title: Why some PSMA radioligand patients never make it to cycle two
blurb: Looks at whether failure to reach a second cycle of Lu-177-PSMA therapy can be predicted before treatment even starts. The title's own question is basically the finding: being eligible on paper isn't the same as being likely to actually complete the regimen.

original_title: Escape from flatland: Strained-ring linchpins for 3D heterocyclic scaffolds in drug discovery
title: Breaking heterocycles out of flatland
blurb: The pitch is using strained-ring building blocks as linchpins to get real 3D shape into heterocyclic scaffolds, instead of the flat aromatic cores most drug discovery libraries default to.

original_title: In Situ Generated Difluoroketene as a C1 Synthon for the [4 + 1] Annulation to 5-Difluoromethyl-1,2,4-oxadiazoles
title: Difluoroketene made to order, then annulated into oxadiazoles
blurb: Difluorobromoacetylsilane generates difluoroketene in situ as a one-carbon synthon, which then does a [4+1] annulation with amidoximes to build 5-difluoromethyl-1,2,4-oxadiazoles. Mild conditions and broad substrate tolerance, and it holds up at gram scale with downstream derivatization, so this reads like an actual building-block method rather than a one-substrate curiosity.

original_title: Tetraxene: Serendipity Leads to a Versatile Three‐Dimensional Building Block
title: A COT scaffold found by accident, kept on purpose
blurb: Tetraxene, a tetraindene-fused cyclooctatetraene scaffold, turned up while trying to push truxene's conjugation further, not from a planned route to it. Indanone condensations want to collapse straight into the thermodynamic trimer, so the fix was catching and reactivating a dimer intermediate before it got there, redirecting the whole reaction toward the new scaffold. Serendipity doing the heavy lifting, not design.

original_title: Direct Characterization of Polysaccharides with In-Source Derivatization and Tandem Mass Spectrometry
title: DART-MS skips the prep work on polysaccharides
blurb: Online methylation with TMAH right in a DART ion source methylates and fragments polysaccharides on the fly, skipping the slow derivatization and cleanup these structures usually demand. Ambient and fast enough to be high-throughput, which matters given how heterogeneous polysaccharides normally make this kind of characterization.

original_title: Theranostic Imaging Agents: Integrating Molecular Diagnostics, Precision Therapeutics, and Artificial Intelligence.
title: Theranostics, now with AI bolted on
blurb: A review stitching together molecular diagnostics, precision therapeutics, and AI under the theranostic imaging umbrella. No new data, just a case for where the field's heading.

original_title: Visible-light-Enabled O-Selective Radical Etherification of 1,2-Dicarbonyl Compounds for the Synthesis of Sterically Congested Ethers
title: Light-driven etherification gets you the ethers that are a pain to make
blurb: Visible-light radical chemistry on 1,2-dicarbonyl compounds, steered to react through oxygen rather than carbon, builds sterically congested ethers that are usually awkward to put together directly.

original_title: Metastable Adducts as a Route to Silver Thiolate Processing on the Way to New Thiorenes: Structural, Spectroscopy, and Computational Data
title: Silver thiolates via a detour through metastable adducts
blurb: Fluorinated aryl silver thiolates, [Ag(S-ArF)]n, recrystallized out of pyridine and its derivatives instead of made directly, giving 1D coordination polymer chains, [(py-R)Ag(S-ArF)]n. That one recrystallization trick yielded seventeen new complexes, backed by structural, spectroscopic, and computational data, on the way to a new thiorene class of metal-organic chalcogenides.

original_title: Mechanistic Insights into Nicotinamidase by CoII EPR Spectroscopy
title: Swapping in cobalt to watch nicotinamidase actually work
blurb: Nicotinamidase normally runs on spectroscopically silent Zn(II), so swapping in Co(II) for SpPncA from Streptococcus pneumoniae gives EPR a handle on the mechanism. Worth the trouble because the enzyme is essential in pathogens but absent in mammals, which makes it one of those clean antibiotic targets if the catalytic details ever get pinned down.

original_title: Multibatch Analysis of Process Sensitivity Across Stages in 100 g Scale Mannose Triflate Synthesis.
title: Scaling mannose triflate to 100 grams without losing the plot
blurb: A multibatch look at where process sensitivity actually creeps in across the stages of mannose triflate synthesis at 100 g scale, the unglamorous precursor-scale-up work that decides whether a route someone liked at gram scale survives going bigger.

original_title: Hyaluronic acid-functionalized polypyrrole nanoparticles with controlled oxidation for targeted chemo-photothermal therapy of prostate cancer
title: Dialing in polypyrrole nanoparticle oxidation for photothermal therapy
blurb: Hyaluronic acid-coated polypyrrole nanoparticles for combined chemo-photothermal therapy in prostate cancer, with oxidative defect density tuned via oxidant concentration during polymerization or post-synthesis reduction. More oxidative defects means worse photothermal performance, an inverse relationship clean enough to work as a dial for the particles' heat output.

original_title: Radioligand Therapy in Oligometastatic Prostate Cancer and the LUNAR Trial - Amar Kishan - UroToday
title: Radioligand therapy angling for oligometastatic prostate cancer
blurb: Amar Kishan's case for using radioligand therapy in oligometastatic prostate cancer, framed around the LUNAR trial. It's commentary making the argument for the approach rather than a readout of new results.

original_title: Zymeworks Presents New Phase 1 Data for Folate Receptor Alpha-Targeting Antibody-Drug Conjugate ZW191 at ESMO Congress 2026 - Yahoo Finance
title: Zymeworks' FRα ADC gets a fresh Phase 1 look at ESMO
blurb: New Phase 1 data on ZW191, Zymeworks' antibody-drug conjugate targeting folate receptor alpha, presented at ESMO Congress 2026. Early and the numbers are the company's own, so wait for independent confirmation before reading too much into it.

original_title: Toward a modular label-free electrochemical biosensing platform based on a one-pot avidin functionalization of reduced graphene oxide
title: A graphene oxide reduction that loads its own avidin as it goes
blurb: One pot, ultrasound-assisted: L-tyrosine and ascorbic acid partially reduce graphene oxide while avidin gets built in during the same step, skipping a separate functionalization stage. The trick is restoring enough of the carbon framework for conductivity while leaving enough oxygen groups behind to still anchor biotinylated probes, which is usually the tradeoff this chemistry fights.

original_title: CD44-Targeted Antibody-Drug Conjugates Suppress Ovarian Tumor Progression and Remodels Cancer Stem Cell-Associated Molecular Programs.
title: A CD44-targeted ADC that goes after ovarian cancer's stem cells too
blurb: An anti-CD44 antibody-drug conjugate that suppresses ovarian tumor progression and reshapes the molecular programs tied to cancer stem cells, the subpopulation usually blamed for relapse. No model or dosing detail beyond that, but going after the stem-like cells rather than just bulk tumor is the notable part.

original_title: Photoinduced Charge Separation via Symmetry-Breaking
title: Trying to find one rulebook behind symmetry-breaking charge separation
blurb: A review arguing that symmetry-breaking charge separation, normally described system by system, actually fits one framework once you plot electronic coupling, driving force, and nuclear reorganization together. It's a synthesis across existing systems rather than a new result, but a unifying picture instead of twenty disconnected case studies is worth something.

original_title: Dosimetry Data Infrastructure for Individualized Radiopharmaceutical Therapy: International Experience and a Proposed Framework for China.
title: China wants its own dosimetry data infrastructure for radiopharma therapy
blurb: A proposed framework for building out dosimetry data infrastructure in China for individualized radiopharmaceutical therapy, drawing on how other countries have done it. A policy and infrastructure proposal, not new trial data.

original_title: Bi(OTf)3-Catalyzed Diastereoselective Three-Component Povarov Reaction of Aminoquinones toward Tetrahydroquinolinequinones
title: A Bi(OTf)3 Povarov reaction that builds tetrahydroquinolinequinones in one pot
blurb: Aminoquinones, aldehydes, and olefins combine under Bi(OTf)3 catalysis to give tetrahydroquinolinequinones in yields up to 96%, with diastereoselectivity ranging from a shrug-worthy 1.6:1 to over 20:1 depending on substrate. E- and Z-alkene probes point to a stepwise cationic mechanism rather than a concerted cycloaddition, and a follow-up oxidative dehydrogenation opens a route to the fully aromatic quinolinequinones as well.

original_title: Alpha-Emitting Prostate Cancer Therapy 212Pb-ADVC001 Well Tolerated in First-in-Human Trial - Bioengineer.org
title: 212Pb-ADVC001 clears its first human safety hurdle
blurb: An alpha-emitting lead-212 therapy for prostate cancer, ADVC001, comes back well tolerated in its first-in-human trial. Safety data only at this stage, so whether it actually shrinks tumors is still an open question.

original_title: PD-L1-Targeted Lutetium-177 Radiotherapy Shrinks Triple-Negative Breast Tumors in Mice - Bioengineer.org
title: A PD-L1-seeking Lu-177 payload shrinks triple-negative breast tumors, in mice
blurb: Lutetium-177 hitched to a PD-L1-targeting ligand shrinks triple-negative breast tumors in mice. Mouse data only, so the usual gap to a human dose still stands between here and anything clinical.

original_title: Recovery of a Minor Cryo-EM Particle Population Reveals Conformational Equilibria Linking Cofactor Loading, Turnover, and Reactivation in Methionine Synthase
title: Digging the rare cryo-EM particles methionine synthase was hiding
blurb: Reanalyzing an old cryo-EM dataset with a neural-network particle picker and more careful classification turns up a minor population of methionine synthase particles that bulk averaging had washed out. That rare conformer links cofactor loading, turnover, and reactivation, the handoffs between the enzyme's big domain rearrangements that structural work has struggled to pin down.

original_title: 580 ºC organic reaction in 2026 (Ben List's group)
title: 580 ºC organic reaction in 2026 (Ben List's group)
